title: SRE phone screen notes — Jane Doe (candidate)
summary: Phone screen for SRE candidate (Jane Doe). Covered background, recent on-call ownership, incident response, distributed systems basics, and familiarity with inference-serving concepts (adjacent experience via feature-serving + websocket streaming). Candidate communicated clearly and had credible examples (retry storms, circuit breakers, latency/batching tradeoffs, hybrid networking/security work). Next step updated: instead of a take-home, move to a 60-min live technical (debugging + systems design) due to turnaround/time constraints; proceed once references are in.
topics: on-call and incident management experience (postmortems, runbooks, mitigations)
latency + batching + queueing; tail-latency reduction example
distributed systems and serving-adjacent concepts (caching, cold-starts, streaming timeouts)
security/networking: VPN, cert rotation, audit logging, kernel/network tuning
availability, compensation expectations, and interview process
signals_positive: Strong incident response instincts (rate limiting, circuit breakers, isolate retry loops; pragmatic mitigation-first approach).
Hands-on with performance/latency work; can articulate batching/priority-queue tradeoffs.
Comfortable in Linux/network tuning territory for typical SRE work (TCP buffers, net.core; namespaces for isolation).
Has worked in hybrid/VPC-adjacent environments (VPN tunnels, cert rotation, audit logging/compliance).
Clear communication; good at structured postmortems.
signals_risk_or_gaps: No direct LLM inference platform ownership; experience is adjacent (feature-serving + websocket streaming).
Not a deep kernel internals specialist (self-described), though likely sufficient for role.
Need to validate ownership depth via technical round (especially debugging under load + SLO reasoning).
process_notes_updates: Original plan mentioned a short take-home due 2024-11-05. As of 2024-11-06 we switched to a live technical screen (debugging/logging + small systems-design prompt) to reduce candidate burden and speed the loop. References requested during phone screen; candidate offered manager + cross-functional PM.
next_steps: People Ops (Nina Patel): confirm live technical panel + scheduling options (target week of 2024-11-11).
Maya Roberts: provide live technical prompt outline (debugging scenario + reliability tradeoffs) to interviewers.
Jane Doe: send two references (manager + cross-functional PM) and confirm availability.
action_items: Nina Patel: coordinate scheduling for 60-min live technical (debugging + systems design) (target by 2024-11-08).
Liam Chen: refresh evaluation rubric for live technical (replace take-home rubric) (target by 2024-11-08).
Maya Roberts: compile focus areas for technical round (SLOs, retries, backpressure, observability) (target by 2024-11-07).
compensation_and_availability: Availability: ~3-week notice (candidate stated). Compensation: candidate said 'open to market' on call; later recruiting note indicates preference for a total comp band aligned to senior SRE market, but no hard number given in phone screen.
on_call_cadence_note: During Q&A we described SRE rotation as 1 week primary with a backup rotation; cadence discussed as approximately one primary week every ~6 weeks (team of 6) depending on PTO/coverage (correcting earlier shorthand phrasing).
transcript_excerpt:
00:00 Maya: Hi Jane, thanks for taking the time — this is Maya from Redwood Inference, I’m on the SRE team...
01:35 Jane: ...on-call SRE for a self-serve analytics product... led a project to reduce tail latency by ~25% by changing batching and optimizing the queueing layer.
09:50 Jane: I haven't worked on LLM inference specifically, but I’ve handled similar issues in feature-serving: cache warming, cold-start latencies, and streaming timeouts for websockets.
12:30 Jane: We saw a spike caused by a cascading retry loop... introduced rate-limiting and circuit breakers... patched the retry logic.
16:05 Jane: ...hybrid setup... VPN tunnels, cert rotation... compliance for audit logging.
18:45 Jane: ...tuned net.core settings, TCP buffers... used namespaces to isolate test traffic.
29:10 Maya: We'll do a technical exercise focusing on debugging/logging and a small systems-design prompt...
31:25 Maya: ...SRE team of 6; on-call rotates with primary + backup coverage.
notes_to_self: If we move forward: probe for concrete examples of designing alerting to avoid noise, setting SLOs/SLIs, and handling multi-tenant fairness (batching + priority). Also validate collaboration with product/eng during incidents.
